summary: A 1939 Aermotor steel tower with an adjacent 1941 cabin, still staffed every summer and rented out to the public only in winter.

staffing.status: active, staffed every summer and fall season

access.note: Cabin rented only mid-December through late March, since the tower itself is staffed through the warmer months.

visit.trail_note: Winter access only, about 17 miles by snowmobile, skis, or snowshoes; route may not be groomed.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests (Clearwater NF)

events.note: Log cabin ground house added to house lookout staff.
Mr. and Mrs. Daniel McGinnis staffed the tower this year, per the Kellogg Evening News as recorded on Idaho Fire Lookouts' known-staff list.
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, April 6, 2009.

evidence.supports: tower and cabin built, still staffed
evidence.quote: Walde Mountain Lookout has a 100' metal tower built in 1939. A log cabin ground house was added in 1941. The lookout is staffed.
1939 - 100' steel Aermotor 1941 - Log cabin living quarters built The lookout is staffed every year during the summer months.
1972 Mr. & Mrs. Daniel McGinnis (Kellogg Evening News)
Built in 1939, this 100' steel Aermotor tower is staffed every summer.

evidence.supports: cabin built 1941 to house lookout employees, tower still in use
evidence.quote: Walde Lookout Cabin was built in 1941 to house the employees who worked in the adjacent fire lookout, which was built in 1939. The fire lookout is still in use during the summer and fall, so the cabin is only available for rent from approximately mid-December through late March.
Guests must reach the cabin by snowmobile, skis or snowshoes. This is a trip of around 17 miles, and guests are responsible for their own travel arrangements and safety.
This 14x16-ft. log cabin accommodates four people with two mattresses located in a loft area and two cots.

evidence.supports: elevation and location on watershed divide
evidence.quote: The cabin sits at an elevation of 5,220 feet on the watershed divide between the Lochsa and Clearwater Rivers.
